suggestions.rationale: A sufficiently severe or prolonged urethral stricture can create urinary outflow obstruction and, in some patients, upper-tract dilation including hydronephrosis. The relationship requires objective evidence that the stricture produced clinically significant obstruction and that other causes of hydronephrosis are less likely.

pathwayIntelligence.causalChain: Documented urethral stricture → clinically significant urinary outflow obstruction/back-pressure → claimed hydronephrosis.
developmentQuestions: Is the urethral stricture objectively documented, including location, length, severity, and treatment history?
Is hydronephrosis confirmed by renal ultrasound, CT, or other appropriate imaging?
Were urinary retention, elevated post-void residuals, reduced urinary flow, or other objective signs of obstruction present when hydronephrosis developed?
Are alternative causes such as ureteral obstruction, stones, bladder dysfunction, prostatic obstruction, tumor, or congenital abnormalities documented or excluded?
Did hydronephrosis improve after relief of the urethral obstruction, if follow-up imaging is available?
issuesToResolve: Most urethral strictures do not necessarily produce hydronephrosis; severity, duration, and obstruction must be established in the individual case.
Hydronephrosis has multiple possible causes, so upper-tract dilation alone does not prove a urethral-stricture nexus.

evidenceGaps: Urology documentation confirming urethral stricture severity and objective obstruction
Imaging confirming hydronephrosis and its timing relative to the stricture
Clinical evaluation addressing alternative upper- or lower-urinary-tract causes and response after obstruction relief

sourceReferences.citation: Renal and ureteral complications of urethral stenosis, PMID 8571802
sourceReferences.note: Clinical series of 180 patients with urethral stenosis reporting renal-ureteral complications including ureterohydronephrosis; supports an obstruction-to-upper-tract-dilation pathway but not automatic individual causation.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 8571802 abstract; ureterohydronephrosis among reported renal-ureteral complications
